blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Model specifications define how large language models (LLMs) should behave, guiding alignment training, inference-time behavior, and evaluation. Yet these specifications may themselves contain defects: two individually reasonable principles may prescribe incompatible behavior when applied to the same situation, leaving no response that satisfies both. Detecting such inconsistencies is challenging. Formalizing natural-language specifications risks losing subtle distinctions, while behavior-based testing cannot reliably distinguish specification defects from differences in model behavior. We introduce VeriSpec , the first approach to directly detect inconsistencies in model specifications by auditing the specification text itself. Our key insight is to preserve the specification in natural language while using an LLM as a verifier. VeriSpec extracts structured, context-aware rules, constructs a topic-guided graph to cluster behaviorally related rules at the same authority level, and applies LLM-as-verifier reasoning to detect inconsistencies. Applying VeriSpec to the OpenAI Model Spec, we extract 405 rules and manually validate five inconsistencies, all reported to its developers, who responded positively and have initiated internal discussions. Compared with five baselines, VeriSpec identifies the most validated inconsistencies, achieves the highest precision (38.5%), and incurs the lowest cost per validated inconsistency ($11.12). These results establish direct specification auditing as a practical complement to behavioral alignment evaluation, catching defects at the source before they shape any model. The code is available at https://github.com/HIPREL-Group/VeriSpec .

blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Model specifications have become a central interface for describing how LLMs should behave. They state requirements for usefulness,
style, safety, security, and legal compliance, and they guide alignment
training, inference-time behavior, and
evaluation ( Bai et al., 2022 ; Guan et al., 2025 ; Wolfe, 2026 ) . Some providers
publish these requirements for external review: OpenAI provides the Model Spec ( OpenAI, 2026d ) and Anthropic provides Claude’s Constitution ( Anthropic, 2026c ) . We refer to such
documents as model specs . As models and deployment expectations
change, these documents are frequently
updated ( OpenAI, 2025b ; Anthropic, 2026d ) , making
systematic review increasingly important.

As model specs grow, they become difficult to audit manually. A principle may
be clear in isolation yet prescribe incompatible behavior once another
applicable principle enters the picture, and the interacting passages may
appear in different sections, depend on authority levels, or be mediated by
exceptions, examples, and other contextual instructions. Model specs also
differ from conventional natural-language requirements: they govern
open-ended interactions, so an inconsistency may surface only when several
principles are applied to the same concrete
situation ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Buyl et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en:
A natural route to detecting such inconsistencies is to translate the
specification into a formal language and apply a formal
verifier ( Merigoux et al., 2021 ; Giannakopoulou et al., 2020 ; Cosler et al., 2023 ) . For model specs, however, translation is precisely where
meaning is lost: the text leans on modal distinctions, e.g., may , must , should , and on permissions, defaults, exceptions, and
soft obligations that formal languages flatten ( Merigoux et al., 2021 ; Guitton et al., 2025 ) . Automating the translation invites errors on
exactly these distinctions, while performing it manually at the scale of a
full specification requires substantial expert
effort ( Yen et al., 2021 ; Giannakopoulou et al., 2020 ; Cosler et al., 2023 ) . Our key insight is to invert the approach: keep the specification in natural
language and use an LLM as the verifier, so that the distinctions
formalization discards become evidence the verifier reasons over.

blocks.en:
To realize this insight, we make the text checkable by splitting the
specification into rules , still in natural language, each recording a
principle’s source annotation, authority level, precondition, and
postcondition. Two obstacles remain. First, inconsistency is a property of
rules in context : worked examples, explicit exceptions, and trade-off
guidance elsewhere in the specification routinely dissolve apparent conflicts
between bare rule statements, so a verifier shown only the statements reports
tensions the document already resolves. Second, verifying rules pairwise is
quadratic in the rule inventory, and most pairs govern unrelated behavior, so
nearly all verifier calls would be spent confirming that nothing interacts.
We therefore attach to each rule the context needed to interpret it, and
cluster behaviorally related rules—by the topics of behavior they
govern—into compact analysis units at the same authority level (the
specification’s chain of command already adjudicates conflicts across
levels). Each verifier call then reasons over a focused set of potentially
interacting rules rather than a long document in which the relevant passages
are easily lost ( Liu et al., 2024 ) .

We evaluate VeriSpec on the OpenAI Model Spec ( OpenAI, 2026d ) . VeriSpec extracts 405 rules,
constructs 32 analysis units, and reports 13 candidate inconsistencies after

developers, who responded positively and have initiated internal discussions.

achieves the highest precision at 38.5%, and has the lowest cost per
validated inconsistency at $11.12.

blocks.en: In summary, this paper makes the following contributions: • Formulation. We formalize specification inconsistency at the level of concrete situations, accounting for rule authority and surrounding context. • Approach. We introduce VeriSpec , to our knowledge the first approach to directly detect inconsistencies in natural-language model specifications through context-aware rule extraction, graph-based clustering, and LLM-as-verifier reasoning. • Evaluation. We identify five validated inconsistencies in the OpenAI Model Spec and report them to its developers. Comparisons against five baselines demonstrate the effectiveness of VeriSpec , which achieves the highest precision and the lowest cost per validated inconsistency.

blocks.en: 2 Background: OpenAI Model Spec
blocks.zh: 2 背景: OpenAI 模型光谱

blocks.en:
Principles in the model spec are organized into a hierarchy of sections by theme, such as prohibitions, usefulness, and style.
Principles may state hard boundaries that should not be compromised, defaults for unspecified preferences, or decision rubrics for gray areas. The model spec also includes concrete examples that demonstrate how certain principles should be applied in practice.
blocks.zh:
模型类别中的原则按主题,如禁止、用途和风格,分成几节。
原则可能规定硬界限,不应损害,未具体说明的偏好默认,或灰色区域的决定标题。 示范项目还包括具体的例子,说明在实践中应如何适用某些原则。

blocks.en:
Authority levels. Each section in the model spec is labeled with an authority level : root, system, developer, user, or guideline. Sections thus form a chain of command, with root-level sections at the top and sections from other levels
progressively below. In other words, principles from higher-level sections take precedence in case of conflicts ( Wallace et al., 2024 ; OpenAI, 2026d ; Wolfe, 2026 ) .

逐渐降低。 换句话说,在发生冲突时,上级部门的原则优先(Wallace等人,2024年;OpenAI,2026d;Wolfe,2026年).

However, not all principles are annotated in this way. We address this in Section 4.1.1 . Figure 2 illustrates these annotations for our

blocks.en: 3 Related Work
blocks.zh: 3 相关工作

blocks.en:
Evaluating Model Alignment. A model specification describes the intended behavior of models, not the
behavior deployed systems exhibit, so alignment to a specification is
typically evaluated empirically after deployment. Ahmed et al. (2025) audit models against provider specifications by
parsing behavioral statements, generating targeted prompts, and using models
as judges. OpenAI similarly provides an evaluation pipeline and prompt
dataset for measuring adherence to the Model Spec ( Guo and Wolfe, 2026 ) . Jakkli et al. (2026) study whether models follow their
provider specifications across generations, and Wang et al. (2026) synthesize specification-alignment data to improve model behavior. All of
these works take the specification as ground truth and ask whether models
comply with it. We invert the question: we treat the specification itself as
the object of analysis and ask whether that ground truth is internally
consistent.

blocks.en:
Value Conflicts in Model Behavior. A second line of work studies how models prioritize competing values. Buyl et al. (2025) show that arbitrary behavioral-value annotations
can lead models away from human discretion, while Liu et al. (2026) use value-conflict scenarios to test
prioritization and show that detailed value rankings can improve alignment.
These papers ask how models behave when values compete; we ask a prior
question: whether the written specification prescribes incompatible behavior
in the first place, before it is used to train, evaluate, or guide any model.

blocks.en:
Behavior-Based Specification Testing. The closest line of work uses model behavior to stress-test the specification
itself. Zhang et al. (2025) generate value-tradeoff scenarios,
measure disagreement across frontier LLMs, and evaluate OpenAI models against
the OpenAI Model Spec, showing that behavioral disagreement can surface
possible specification issues. This signal, however, is indirect and can err
in both directions. The Model Spec and deployed models evolve on separate
schedules, and the specification version used to train or align a given model
is unknown ( OpenAI, 2026b ) ; OpenAI itself notes that deployed
behavior may diverge from the Model Spec ( OpenAI, 2025a ) . A
behavioral disagreement may therefore reflect training, alignment, or
capability differences rather than a specification
defect ( Ahmed et al., 2025 ; Guo and Wolfe, 2026 ; Jakkli et al., 2026 ) —and, conversely, a defect that models
happen to resolve the same way produces no disagreement to observe. To our
knowledge, VeriSpec is the first approach to detect model specification defects
directly: it audits the specification text rather than the behavior it
induces, and reports concrete inconsistencies supported by structured
verifier reasoning and manual validation.

blocks.en: 4 Methodology
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en:
VeriSpec detects internal inconsistencies in model specifications through the
three-stage pipeline shown in Figure 3 . Context-aware rule extraction (Section 4.1 ) makes the specification checkable: it
converts every principle into a structured natural-language rule and
attaches the context (e.g., worked examples, exceptions, trade-off
guidance) needed to interpret it. Graph-based rule clustering (Section 4.2 ) makes verification tractable: over a
topic-guided rule graph, it clusters behaviorally related rules into

blocks.en: Anonymization. Model specifications contain many references to the corresponding model provider and its models, such as OpenAI and GPT-4.1. Proprietary LLMs often refuse to analyze model specifications in depth since these references trigger their safety guardrails. We found that anonymizing the model specification, i.e., replacing these references with synthetic names, suppresses guardrails and allows us to analyze the model specification. We used Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025 ) to perform the anonymization, together with static checks to ensure that edits are limited to such substitutions.

blocks.en:
As described in Section 2 , many principles in the model spec have alphanumeric annotations called focus areas . These annotations provide anchors in the specification, allowing us to systematically cover all principles in the model spec.
The model spec contains 279 annotations, but we found by manual inspection that many principles are not annotated and a small number of annotations
do not even mark principles. The latter only adds a small amount of overhead during analysis, but the former limits coverage by omitting principles that may be involved in inconsistencies.

blocks.en:
Note that a statement in the model spec is considered to be a principle if it prescribes model behavior in some situation. A statement may contain multiple principles, in which case each of them should carry its own annotation. Following this criterion, we used the existing annotations as examples to guide Claude Code in annotating the remaining principles and thus completing the annotations. We added 126 annotations, bringing the total to 405. Figure 2 shows one added annotation for our
running example (Figure 1 ).

blocks.en: We use the LLM as a verifier rather than as an unconstrained inconsistency detector. We use Claude Opus 5 ( Anthropic, 2026b ) as the core verifier because it reliably follows the structured verification prompt and completes the full analysis units; GPT-6 Astra ( OpenAI, 2026a ) produced similar findings at higher cost, while Claude Fable 5.1 ( Anthropic, 2026a ) blocked most requests under Anthropic’s restrictions on violative cyber content. For each analysis unit, the verifier receives the rules in that unit together with the context needed to interpret them. A valid report must provide evidence for Definition 3 : it must give a concrete witness situation, explain why both rules apply, and justify why the combined context does not resolve the inconsistency.

blocks.en: The verifier does not compare rules by surface form. blocks.zh: 精细. 部分报告的不一致之处经过人工验证。

blocks.en: Cost. The total cost of running the method.
blocks.zh: 费用。 运行该方法的总成本.

blocks.en: Cost per validated inconsistency. The total cost divided by the number of validated inconsistencies, reported only when a method validates at least one inconsistency.
blocks.zh: 按经核实的不一致情况计算的费用。 费用总额除以经核实的不一致的数目,只有在一种方法至少证实一种不一致时才报告。

blocks.en: We report cost because methods may improve detection quality by issuing more LLM requests, so the comparison should reflect both detection quality and resource use.
blocks.zh: 我们报告费用是因为方法可能会通过发出更多的LLM请求来提高检测质量,因此比较应反映检测质量和资源使用情况.

blocks.en: Inconsistency validation. We validate each reported inconsistency through manual inspection by two reviewers. Each reviewer independently examines the reported rule pair, witness, and supporting context, and assigns a verdict on whether the report is a true inconsistency. When the two verdicts agree, we use the agreed verdict as the final label. When they disagree, the reviewers discuss the case and assign a final consensus verdict.
blocks.zh: 前后不一致的论证. 通过两名审查员的人工检查,我们验证了每一份报告的不一致之处。 每个审查员独立审查所报告的规则对子、证人和支助背景,并对报告是否真正不一致作出判断。 当两个判决达成一致时,我们使用商定的判决作为最终标签. 当他们不同意时,审查人员将讨论案件,并作出最终协商一致的裁决。

blocks.en: Baselines. We compare VeriSpec against baselines that remove or simplify different parts of the pipeline. To ensure a fair comparison, all methods are powered by Claude Opus 5 and are run for five attempts, matching the repeated detection budget used by VeriSpec . We did not find an existing tool that directly targets inconsistency detection for model specifications, so these baselines are constructed from natural alternatives. Table 1 summarizes the comparison, and Appendix C provides additional implementation details.
blocks.zh: 基线。 我们比较VeriSpec和去除或简化管道不同部分的基线。 为了保证公平比较,所有的方法都由克劳德·奥普斯5(英语:Claude Opus 5)提供动力,并运行五次尝试,与VeriSpec使用的反复检测预算相匹配. 我们没有找到一个现有工具直接针对模型规格的不一致性检测,因此这些基线是用自然替代品构建的。 表1汇总了比较情况,附录C提供了其他执行细节。

blocks.en: • DirectAgent . We give the full specification to a fresh Claude Code agent and ask it to find inconsistencies. This baseline tests whether a general-purpose coding agent can perform the detection without the structure introduced by VeriSpec . • DirectPrompt . We give the full specification to the LLM in a single prompt and ask it to report inconsistencies directly. This baseline tests whether a non-agentic whole-spec prompt is sufficient without rule extraction, graph construction, or LLM-as-verifier detection. • SectionText . We remove the rule extraction phase, use each source section as an analysis unit, and apply LLM-as-verifier detection directly to the section text. This baseline tests whether explicit rule extraction is necessary, or whether the source text alone is sufficient. • SectionGroup . We keep the rule extraction phase and LLM-as-verifier detection, but form the analysis units by source section instead of by the rule graph. This baseline tests whether the document structure alone is sufficient to form analysis units. • PlainDetect . We use the same analysis units VeriSpec uses but ask the LLM to detect inconsistencies directly rather than using LLM-as-verifier detection. This baseline tests the effect of LLM-as-verifier detection.

blocks.zh: 节图文集. 我们取消了规则提取阶段,将每个源段用作分析单元,并将LLM-as-验证器检测直接应用到该部分文本中. 这种基线检验是否有必要明确规则提取,或仅凭源文本是否足够。

blocks.en: 5.2 Main Results
blocks.zh: 5.2 主要成果

blocks.en: Applying VeriSpec to the 405 extracted rules produced 32 same-authority analysis units. We ran inconsistency detection five times on each unit, yielding 160 independent detection requests. Across these runs, VeriSpec produced 17 raw inconsistency reports. After removing duplicate outputs and merging reports that described the same specification inconsistency, we obtained 13 candidate inconsistencies for manual inspection. Figure 4 shows that the cumulative number of unique candidate inconsistencies saturates at the fifth attempt, where all candidates have been found.
blocks.zh: 将VeriSpec应用于405条提取的规则,产生了32个同授权分析单元. 我们在每个单位进行了五次不一致性检测,结果收到160项独立检测请求。 在整个过程中,VeriSpec编写了17份原始的不一致报告。 在删除重复的产出和合并说明同一规格不一致的报告之后,我们获得了13项供手工检查的候选不一致之处。 图4显示,在已找到所有候选人的第五次尝试中,候选人独特不一致的累积数量饱和。

blocks.en: Figure 4: Cumulative candidate inconsistencies across detection attempts.
blocks.zh: 图4:各种检测尝试中候选人累积的不一致情况。

blocks.en: Figure 5: Reported and validated inconsistencies by authority.
blocks.zh: 图5:按当局报告和核实的不一致情况。

blocks.en: Manual inspection validated 5 of the 13 candidates, giving VeriSpec a precision of 38.5% at a total cost of $55.62. Figure 5 shows that the validated inconsistencies come from system- and user-level rules, while root- and guideline-level candidates are filtered out during validation. The 5 validated inconsistencies span legal constraints, code transformations, output-only tasks, fictional portrayals, and sycophantic reassurance, showing that specification defects arise from both local and cross-section rule interactions. We have reported these 5 inconsistencies to the OpenAI Model Spec developers. Figure 1 shows the code-transformation inconsistency as the running example, and Section 5.4 presents the other four validated inconsistencies.
blocks.zh: 人工检查验证了13名候选人中的5名,使VeriSpec精确度达到38.5%,总费用为55.62美元. 图5显示,经验证的不一致来自系统和用户层面的规则,而根和准则层面的候选人则在验证过程中被过滤出. 这5个经验证的不一致之处跨越了法律限制,代码转换,只输出任务,虚构的描述,以及sycophantic的保证,表明规格缺陷来自局部和横截面规则相互作用. 我们已经向OpenAI模型Spec开发者报告了这5个不一致之处. 图1以代码转换不一致为运行示例,第5.4节则列出其他四个经验证的不一致.

blocks.en: 5.3 Baseline Comparison
blocks.zh: 5.3 基线比较

blocks.en: Table 1 compares VeriSpec with the baselines. Among the baselines, PlainDetect finds the most validated inconsistencies with 3, while SectionGroup achieves the highest precision at 12.5%. DirectAgent and DirectPrompt cost less than VeriSpec , but neither reports any validated inconsistency. VeriSpec has the lowest cost per validated inconsistency at $11.12, compared with $15.82 for PlainDetect and more than $58 for the section-based verifier baselines.
blocks.zh: 表1 比较 具有基线的VeriSpec. 在基线中,Plain Detection发现最经验证的不一致之处为3,而SectionGroup的精度最高,为12.5%。 DirectAgent and DirectPrompt 成本低于 VeriSpec ,但两者都没有报告任何经证实的不一致之处. VeriSpec每经核实的不一致情况费用最低,为11.12美元,而Plain Detection为15.82美元,以科为基础的核查基线为58美元以上。

blocks.en: Whole-specification detection is not sufficient. DirectAgent and DirectPrompt give the model access to the full specification, but neither produces a validated inconsistency. They report 9 and 16 candidates respectively, all of which fail manual validation. A recurring failure mode is to report an inconsistency after reading only the apparent tension between two passages, while missing a nearby exception that resolves the pair. In one false report, the baseline treated a transformation permission as inconsistent with content prohibitions, even though the transformation passage explicitly says that the permission still applies when the transformed output would otherwise be restricted. This result shows that whole-specification access alone does not focus the model on the specific principles that may be inconsistent, and it does not force the model to check whether the surrounding context resolves a candidate inconsistency.
blocks.zh: 整体规格检测不足. DirectAgent and DirectPrompt让模型访问到完整的规格,但两者都没有产生经过验证的不一致. 他们分别报告9名和16名候选人,所有这些候选人都未能通过人工验证。 一个反复出现的失败模式是在只读出两段之间的明显张力后报告不一致,同时缺少一个解决对对的附近例外. 在一份虚假报告中,基线将变换许可视为不符合内容禁令,尽管变换通道明确规定,变换输出否则会受到限制时,该许可仍然适用. 这一结果表明,仅靠整体特异性访问并不能使模型专注于可能不一致的具体原则,也不迫使模型检查周围上下文是否解决了候选不一致.

blocks.en: Section-based grouping misses cross-section cases. SectionText and SectionGroup validate only one inconsistency each, namely the legal-disclosure case whose two rules appear in the same section. They miss cases whose rules are distributed across the document, including the code-transformation case used as the running example in Figure 1 . The difference between SectionText and SectionGroup is also small, which suggests that rule extraction helps most when paired with analysis units that group rules by behavior rather than by source section.
blocks.zh: 基于科的分组错过了交叉案件。 该科和科组只确认各有一个不一致之处,即法律披露案,其两条规则载于同一节。 它们错过了规则在整个文件中分发的案件,包括图1中用作运行实例的代码转换案件。 科Text与科Group的区别也很小,这表明规则提取在与分析单位对齐时最有帮助,这些分析单位根据行为而不是源节来进行分组规则.

blocks.en: LLM-as-verifier detection reduces false positives. PlainDetect uses the same rule-graph units as VeriSpec but asks the LLM to report inconsistencies directly. It finds 3 validated inconsistencies, but it reports 221 candidates and achieves only 1.4% precision. Most invalid reports are resolved by specification context, including explicit exceptions, compatible joint responses, worked examples, or the chain of command. The LLM-as-verifier detection targets this failure mode by requiring a witness, an unsatisfiability argument, and a context-resolution argument before reporting. This reduces the candidate set from 221 to 13 while increasing precision from 1.4% to 38.5%.
blocks.zh: LLM-as-验证器检测可以减少假阳性. Plain Detect使用与VeriSpec相同的规则图单位,但要求LLM直接报告不一致. 它发现了3个经验证的不一致之处,但它报告了221名候选人,并且只实现了1.4%。 大多数无效报告都通过规格上下文解决,包括明确的例外、兼容的联合答复、工作实例或指挥链。 LLM-as-验证器检测以这种故障模式为目标,在报告前要求有目击证人,不满意论证,以及上下文解析论证. 这使候选人从221人减少到13人,同时精确度从1.4%增加到38.5%。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented VeriSpec , an approach to directly detecting
inconsistencies in natural-language model specifications
through context-aware rule extraction, graph-based clustering,
and LLM-as-verifier reasoning. Applied to the OpenAI Model
Spec, VeriSpec identified five manually validated inconsistencies
and outperformed five baselines in detection precision and
cost per validated inconsistency. These findings demonstrate
that systematic auditing can uncover defects in the
specifications themselves, complementing existing approaches
that evaluate model behavior.

Spec, VeriSpec 发现了五个手动验证的不一致之处

系统审计可以发现

评估模型行为。

blocks.en:
Our work opens a broader direction toward continuous
verification and improvement of model specifications.
As these specifications evolve, future research can extend
beyond inconsistency detection to automated specification
repair, incremental verification, and systematic auditing
across different model providers. More fundamentally, our
work challenges a prevailing assumption in LLM alignment:
that the specifications against which models are trained
and evaluated can themselves be treated as ground truth.
Ensuring that models follow their specifications is only
part of the challenge; ensuring that those specifications
are themselves consistent is equally important.

blocks.en: Appendix A Rule Inventory Construction
blocks.zh: 附录A

blocks.en: This appendix gives details omitted from the main description of rule extraction. We describe how we decide which missing principles receive annotations, how we choose annotation granularity, how we validate the extracted inventory, and how we handle authority labels for container sections.
blocks.zh: 本附录提供了规则提取主要描述中省略的细节. 我们描述我们如何决定哪些缺失的原则得到说明,我们如何选择注释颗粒性,我们如何验证提取的库存,以及我们如何处理容器部分的权威标签。

blocks.en: Annotation criterion. We add a missing annotation only when the statement prescribes model behavior in a situation. This includes requirements, recommendations, prohibitions, and explicit permissions. The statement must be directed at the assistant, and the governed situation and behavior must be specific enough for compliance to be judged. Modal verbs alone are not sufficient: “the assistant may refuse” grants a permission and is therefore a principle, whereas “the assistant may encounter errors” describes a possibility and is not. We do not annotate example conversations, commentary, definitions, rationales, restatements of already annotated principles, or statements that govern parties other than the assistant. Existing focus-area annotations are preserved, so the completion pass only adds missing annotations.
blocks.zh: 注释标准。 我们只当声明规定了某种情况下的示范行为时,才会添加一个缺失的注释. 这包括要求、建议、禁令和明确许可。 声明必须针对助理,治理的情况和行为必须足够具体,以便判断是否遵守. 单凭动词是不够的:“助理可以拒绝”给予许可,因此是一项原则,而“助理可能遇到错误”则描述一种可能性,而不是。 我们不注意实例性谈话、评论、定义、理由、已附加说明的原则的重申,或对辅助方以外的当事方适用的声明。 现有的焦点领域说明保留下来,因此完成传只增加了缺失的说明.

blocks.en: Annotation granularity. We follow the granularity of the original annotations. A normative sentence is normally treated as one principle, even when it lists several coordinated actions or conditions. We split a sentence only when it states separable policies, for example when the polarity changes or when neighboring original annotations already mark parallel items separately. A qualification that narrows a principle stays with that principle, while a clause that permits otherwise restricted behavior is treated as a separate principle. In the completed annotation set, 26 sentences carry more than one annotation; 23 of these splits were already present in the original model spec.
blocks.zh: 注释颗粒性. 我们遵循原始说明的颗粒性。 规范性句子通常被视为一项原则,即使它列出了几项协调行动或条件。 我们只当它说出可分离的政策时,例如当极性改变或当邻近的原注已经分别标出平行项目时,才分句. 缩小一项原则的限定与这项原则一致,而允许以其他方式限制行为的条款则被视为一项单独的原则。 在完成的注解集中,26句包含不止一个注解;其中23个分解在原型号谱中已经存在.

blocks.en: Annotation review. After the initial annotation pass, we reviewed each section for missed principles and over-fragmented sentences. The original annotations remain unchanged. A static check verifies that the completion pass only inserts annotations and does not otherwise alter the specification text. Table 2 summarizes the original and added annotations by authority level.
blocks.zh: 注释检讨. 在最初的注解通过之后,我们审查了每一节中漏掉的原则和过于分散的句子。 原始说明保持不变。 静态检查验证完成通过时只插入说明,而不改变规格文本。 表2按权力级别汇总了原始说明和补充说明。

blocks.en: Table 2: Original and added annotations by authority level.
blocks.zh: 表2:按主管部门分列的原文和补充说明。

blocks.en: Rule extraction and validation. We use Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025 ) to extract the structured fields for each completed annotation, including the precondition P P , postcondition Q Q , source statement, section path, and associated examples. We then validate the extracted inventory with static checks. The first check enforces one-to-one coverage between annotations and rules, so every annotation appears exactly once and no rule id is duplicated or missing. The second check confirms that each extracted rule remains linked to its source statement and examples, which lets later graph construction recover the context used to interpret P P and Q Q .
blocks.zh: 规则提取与验证. 我们使用Claude Code(Anthropic, 2025)来提取每个已完成注释的结构字段, 包括先决条件 P P, 附加条件 Q Q, 源语句, 节路, 和相关的例子 。 然后我们用静态检查来验证提取的存货 第一个检查在说明和规则之间执行一对一的覆盖,因此每条注释都准确出现一次,没有规则id重复或缺失. 第二次检查证实,每个提取的规则仍然与其源声明和示例相关,这样可以让以后的图形构建恢复用于解释PP和QQ的上下文.

blocks.en: Authority resolution. A rule inherits its authority from the nearest enclosing section with an authority label. This resolves 398 of the 405 rules. The remaining 7 rules appear under unlabelled container headings whose subsections carry different authorities. We resolve these cases manually from the rule wording and the subsections governed by the container. This assigns 6 rules to root authority and 1 rule to system authority.
blocks.zh: 权威决议。 一条规则从最近的附有当局标签的部分继承其权威。 这解决了405条中的398条. 其余7条规则出现在未加标签的集装箱标题下,其分节具有不同的权威。 我们从规则措词和集装箱的分节中人工解决这些案件。 这给根权威分配了6条规则,给系统权威分配了1条规则.

blocks.en: Topic registry. Three independent LLM subagents propose candidate topics and yes/no membership tests ( topic tests ). After merging equivalent tests, we obtain 18 candidate topics, 16 of which are proposed by all three agents. Two subagents then independently apply each test to a sample of 40 rules. We revise tests whose agreement falls below Cohen’s κ = 0.6 \kappa=0.6 and drop topics that remain below it; the only failing test improves from κ = 0.48 \kappa=0.48 to κ = 0.925 \kappa=0.925 after revision, so no topic is dropped. Uncovered rules motivate two additional topics, yielding the 20 topics in Table 4 . An independent closure pass finds no missing topic. To validate the registry against held-out evidence, we remove cross-reference links from the text shown to the agents and later check whether cross-referenced rule pairs receive shared topics. Such pairs share a topic 7.16 × 7.16\times more often than random pairs (permutation test, p ≤ 0.001 p\leq 0.001 ). Seven topics contain more than 30 rules, so we refine them into sub-topics with the same procedure (inter-subagent κ ≥ 0.87 \kappa\geq 0.87 ). The final registry contains 45 leaf topics, consisting of 32 sub-topics and 13 unrefined topics.
blocks.zh: 专题登记。 3名独立的LLM子代理人提出候选题目和是/否会员考试(专题测试). 在合并了同等考试后,我们获得了18个候选题目,其中16个题目都是由三个代理人提出的. 然后两个副剂独立地将每个测试应用于40个规则的样本. 我们修改其协议低于Cohen = 0.6\kappa = 0.6的测试,并删除仍低于该测试的题目;唯一的失败的测试改进从 = 048\kappa = 0.48 到 = 0.925\kappa = 0.925 修改后,不放弃话题。 未覆盖的规则促使增加了两个专题,产生了表4中的20个专题。 独立关闭通行证找不到缺少的话题 。 为了对照搁置的证据对登记处进行验证,我们从向代理人显示的案文中删除了相互参照链接,并随后检查相互参照的规则对是否接收了共同的专题。 这种对子分享一个话题7.16×7.16\时间比随机对子更频繁(permutation test, p_001 p\leq 0.001 ). 7个专题包含30多项规则,因此我们将其细化为具有相同程序的子专题(增殖方为0.87\kappa\geq). (原始内容存档于2017-08-06). 0.87. 最后登记册包括45个叶片专题,包括32个分专题和13个未经修改的专题。

blocks.en: Topic assignment. Applying the membership tests to the 405 rules produces 625 rule–topic nodes. A total of 162 rules receive more than one topic because they govern multiple behaviors. For 21 rules, no test fits clearly. We record these rules as residue and assign each one to its closest topic so that every rule remains covered. Most residue rules describe how conflicts between instructions are resolved, which the registry excludes by design.
blocks.zh: 专题任务。 将会员资格测试应用于405规则产生625个规则-专题节点. 共有162条规则接收了多个话题,因为它们规范了多种行为. 对于21条规则来说,没有测试明显适合. 我们把这些规则记录为残余,并将每一条规则分配给其最密切的专题,以便保留每一条规则。 多数残余规则都描述了如何解决指示之间的冲突,而登记处从设计上排除了这一点。

blocks.en: Analysis units. Table 3 summarizes the resulting graph. Grouping nodes by authority and topic initially produces 113 non-empty groups. The groups are uneven, with 101 groups containing fewer than 12 nodes and many containing only one or two rules. Such small groups give the verifier few rules to compare while still requiring a separate request. We therefore merge small groups within each authority level. Each group below 12 nodes is merged into the same-authority group with which it shares the most rules and graph edges, as long as the merged group has at most 28 nodes. This produces the 32 analysis units used in the experiments, with 14 at the root level, 8 at the user level, 8 at the guideline level, and one each at the system and developer levels.
blocks.zh: 分析组。 表3汇总了得出的图表。 按权威和主题分组的节点最初产生113个非空格组. 团体不均匀,101个团体的节点不足12个,许多团体只包含一条或两条规则. 这种小团体给核查人以很少的规则来比较,同时仍然需要单独提出请求。 因此,我们合并了各级权力机构中的小组。 12个节点以下的每个组被合并为它与它共享最多规则和图边的同一授权组,只要合并组最多拥有28个节点. 这产生了实验中使用的32个分析单元,其中根层14个,用户层8个,准则层8个,系统和开发者层各一个.

blocks.zh: 附录C 执行细节

blocks.en: All methods use Claude Opus 5 and run for five independent attempts, matching the detection budget used by VeriSpec . For direct LLM calls, we use high reasoning effort. DirectAgent is instantiated with Claude Code powered by Claude Opus 5, so it differs from the other baselines in execution but not in the model used.
blocks.zh: 所有方法都使用Claude Opus 5并运行5个独立尝试,与VeriSpec所使用的检测预算相匹配. 对于直接的LLM电话,我们使用高推理努力. DirectAgent由克劳德·奥普斯5(英语:Claude Opus 5)提供动力的Claude Code进行即时处理,因此它与其他执行中的基线不同,但在所使用的模型中则不同.

blocks.en: DirectAgent and DirectPrompt . Both whole-specification baselines receive the anonymized specification once per attempt and do not receive extracted rules, analysis units, or the structured fields required by LLM-as-verifier detection. DirectAgent starts each attempt from a fresh Claude Code session and asks the agent to find internal inconsistencies. DirectPrompt uses a single non-agentic LLM call with the same whole-specification input and task instruction.
blocks.zh: 直接代理和直接Prompt. 整个规格基线每次尝试都得到匿名规格,并且没有获得提取的规则、分析单位或LLM-as-核查器检测所需的结构化字段。 DirectAgent从全新的Claude代码会话开始每次尝试,并要求代理查找内部不一致之处. DirectPrompt使用一个单一的非代理LLM调用,具有相同的全特性输入和任务指令.

blocks.en: SectionText . This baseline removes rule extraction and applies LLM-as-verifier detection directly to source text. We split the specification at second-level headings into 42 units, each consisting of one section with its subsections and examples, and remove annotation tags from the input. The prompt includes the same inconsistency definition and authority background used by VeriSpec . Because the text contains no rule identifiers, the model identifies the relevant statements by quoting them.
blocks.zh: 节图文集. 此基准删除规则提取,并将LLM-as-验证器检测直接应用于源文本. 我们把二级标题的规格分为42个单元,每个单元由一节及其分节和示例组成,并从输入中删除注释标记。 该提示包括VeriSpec所使用的相同不一致的定义和权威背景。 由于文本中没有规则标识符,该模型通过引用相关声明来识别相关声明.

blocks.en: SectionGroup . This baseline keeps rule extraction and LLM-as-verifier detection, but replaces rule-graph analysis units with source-section units. We group rules by authority and second-level source section. Groups containing a single rule are skipped because they contain no rule pair to compare, leaving 39 units that cover 399 of the 405 rules.
blocks.zh: 节组. 这个基线保留了规则提取和LLM-as-验证检测,但将规则图分析单元替换为源段单元. 我们按权限和二级源代码分组 包含单一规则的组合被跳过,因为它们没有包含规则对来比较,留下39个单元,覆盖405规则中的399个单元.

blocks.en: PlainDetect . This baseline keeps the same extracted rules, contexts, and 32 rule-graph analysis units as VeriSpec , but removes LLM-as-verifier detection. The prompt asks the model to report inconsistent rule pairs directly and to give a free-text explanation, without requiring the witness, unsatisfiability, and context-resolution fields used by VeriSpec .
blocks.zh: 普通探测器。 此基线保留了与VeriSpec相同的提取规则,上下文和32个规则图分析单元,但取消了LLM-as-验证器检测. 该提示要求模型直接报告不一致的规则对,并给出自由文字解释,而不要求证人,不满意,以及VeriSpec使用的上下文解析字段.

blocks.en: Candidate consolidation. We normalize outputs in the same way for all methods. We first remove duplicate reports of the same rule or statement pair across attempts and units, and then merge reports that describe the same specification inconsistency. The merged candidates are the reported inconsistencies in Table 1 .
blocks.zh: 候选人合并。 我们以同样的方式使所有方法的产出正常化。 我们首先将同一规则或声明的重复报告删除,然后将描述同一规格不一致的报告合并。 合并的候选人是表1中报告的不一致情况。
